# Five Competing Architectures

The Awtsmoos can clothe one truth in many vessels that rhyme;
Awtsmoos.com must choose the vessel that stays fastest and clearest through time.

## A — Central public-content graph

One build-time graph feeds sitemap, metadata artifacts, coverage tests, and developer reports.
Pros: one source of truth, strong auditability, future extensibility.
Cons: larger migration from current specialized generators.
Use: incremental destination, not an all-at-once rewrite.

## B — Preserve family generators + add coverage auditor

Keep existing app/game/translation/Heichel/comment modules, add a separate auditor that cross-checks them.
Pros: lowest regression risk, easy incremental rollout.
Cons: duplicated family knowledge remains.
Use: preferred near-term architecture.

## C — Runtime crawler graph

Generate discovery dynamically from live database and registries.
Pros: fresh data.
Cons: latency, failure coupling, N+1 risk, crawler monopolization already observed historically.
Use: reject for broad discovery; reserve for bounded dynamic families.

## D — Static pre-render of every public page

Generate HTML for aliases, Heichels, posts, comments, translations, apps, games.
Pros: crawler simplicity.
Cons: huge build/deploy footprint, duplication, stale dynamic content.
Use: reject as global architecture.

## E — Search-specific parallel pages

Create SEO-only mirror pages for interactive surfaces.
Pros: easy semantic control.
Cons: duplicate identity and canonical complexity.
Use: reject except for rare impossible-to-enrich legacy entrypoints.

## Decision

Use B now while moving toward A: preserve proven family-specific runtime behavior, add a unified audit/coverage layer, strengthen page semantics centrally, and only consolidate generation when evidence proves the migration worth the risk.
